title: Phishing
copy: Fake messages and pages designed to steal credentials or information.
steps: Check the sender and domain independently.
Never use a login link supplied by an unexpected message.
Treat urgency + credential requests as a high-risk combination.

title: Urgency manipulation
copy: Pressure tactics that make you act before you verify.
steps: Pause when a message says 'act now' or threatens immediate consequences.
Verify through an official app, website or known phone number.
A deadline does not make an unverified instruction trustworthy.

title: Impersonation
copy: Attackers pretending to be banks, schools, companies, friends or officials.
steps: Compare the identity with an independent source.
Do not trust logos, caller ID or polished graphics alone.
Ask the real organisation through a channel you found yourself.

title: Suspicious links
copy: Look-alike domains, strange paths, redirects and unexpected login pages.
steps: Read the actual hostname, not just the page title.
Avoid shortened or unexpected links when the stakes are high.
Use SATARK's URL scanner before interacting with a suspicious public page.

title: Payment fraud
copy: Fake fees, refunds, prizes, QR payments and requests for money.
steps: Never pay a 'release fee' just to receive a prize/refund.
Do not scan a QR code merely because a message says it is for receiving money.
Confirm payment requests with the recipient independently.

title: Account takeover
copy: Attempts to obtain passwords, OTPs, recovery codes or session access.
steps: Never share OTPs or recovery codes with a caller or chat contact.
Use the official app/site instead of a supplied login link.
If credentials were exposed, change them through the official service immediately.
